newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-YANKEE SS JETER UNANIMOUSLY NAMED AL ROOKIE OF YEAR.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-YANKEE SS JETER UNANIMOUSLY NAMED AL ROOKIE OF YEAR.

text.p: Shortstop Derek Jeter, who
helped the New York Yankees to their first World Series
championship in 18 years, Monday was announced as the
unanimous choice for American League Rookie of the Year.
Jeter was selected first on all 28 ballots in voting by
the Baseball Writers' Association of America. He was the only
player listed on every ballot.
Jeter received 140 points, easily outdistancing Chicago
White Sox pitcher James Baldwin, who received 19 second-place
votes. Jeteris the fifth unanimous AL Rookie of the Year
choice and the first since California's Tim Salmon in 1993.
In his first full season with the Yankees, the 22-year-old
Jeter played outstanding defensively and hit .314 with 10
homers and 78 Runs Batted In, including a .350 average with 40
RBI after the All-Star break. His RBI total was the most by a
rookie shortstop since Julio Franco had 80 for Cleveland in
Jeter is eighth Yankee to win the prestigious first-year
honour and the first since 1981, when pitcher Dave Righetti
claimed the award. The others are Thurman Munson (1970), Stan
Bahnsen (1968), Tom Tresh (1962), Tony Kubek (1957), Bob Grim
(1954) and Gil McDougald (1951).
Baldwin was named on all but two ballots, receiving 64
points. He was 11-6 with a 4.42 ERA.
Detroit Tigers first baseman Tony Clark, who had 27 homers
and 72 RBI, finished third in the balloting with six
second-place votes and 30 points.
The National League Rookie of the Year will be announced
on Wednesday.
The voting breakdown for the 1996 American League Rookie
of the Year Award in balloting by a 28-member panel of the
Baseball Writers' Association of America (five points for
first place, three points for second, one point for third):
